anya: heads-up — we just saw a correlated CPU spike on telemetry-exporter around 15:07 UTC, p99 for span-ingest climbed from 85ms -> 420ms.
sam: saw that in dashboards too. Any recent deploys to exporter or retention jobs? :thinking_face:
mike: retention job rolled out at 15:05 (auto-archive older spans to s3). didn't think it would touch the live exporter path though.
anya: yeah same, retention should be offline. logs show a flurry of exporter warnings at 15:06: `exporter: backpressure=true; flush_loop_time=12ms; queue_len=0; throttle=true`
leah: curious — queue_len=0 and throttle=true seems wrong. maybe retention eviction path is trying to re-emit some traces and hitting the exporter client? can you paste the snippet from the retention worker?
anya: paste below:
```
2026-03-18T15:05:58Z retention-worker INFO archiving batch ids=[...]
2026-03-18T15:06:02Z retention-worker DEBUG enqueue_for_export count=238 service=span-archiver
2026-03-18T15:06:03Z exporter WARN backpressure=true attempt=1 err="connection refused"
2026-03-18T15:06:04Z exporter WARN throttle=true reason="rate limit"
```
sam: whoa, retention-worker seems to be enqueuing archived spans back into the exporter queue (bug). That would spike volume and trigger exporter backpressure and throttle -> CPU spike from retry loops.
mike: confirming: exporter has a per-second token bucket + batching. If retention job accidentally routes archived spans through the same export client (instead of a separate archival pipeline), it will cause retries and p99 blowup.
julian: ops-bot flagged an alert: `telemetry.exporter.p99 > 300ms for 2m` and `exporter.cpu > 70%` and created incident #INC-8306
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-8306 — telemetry exporter overload (see thread)
leah: mitigation idea — temporarily flip retention->archive routing to direct-s3 (avoid exporter) or disable retention worker. Can someone toggle the feature-flag? @mike
mike: toggled ff/retention-archiver to off at 15:10. exporter cpu dropped to 42% within 40s, p99 back under 120ms.
anya: nice rollback. next: fix codepath so retention doesn't reuse the live exporter client. Looks like a shared client ref got passed into archiver by mistake.
sam: adding a unit test + integration test that exercises the archiver with a fake exporter to catch this. also will add a metric `retention.enqueued_to_exporter` to alert earlier.
julian: can we also change retry policy for archival-related exports to be exponential with jitter and much lower concurrency? shouldn't impact live path if misrouted.
leah: agree. i'll file a follow-up RFC for routing separation + retention SLAs.
anya: created PR draft https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412 — contains: (1) split archiver client; (2) new metric; (3) tests. reviewers: @mike @sam
sam: quick note for postmortem: root cause = retention worker erroneously enqueuing archived spans into the real-time exporter queue. contributing factor = lack of integration tests and no metric distinguishing archival vs live exports.
mike: will do a postmortem doc and add runbook step to check retention-job toggles on deploy. thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident INC-8306 resolved by ff toggle at 15:10. CPU and latency recovered.
